text:
martin_support: Heads-up — ACME Ops opened an escalation: after today's rollout their chat completions started returning legacy template text in ~5% of calls. They say the prompts haven't changed. Pasted sample below from customer.

martin_support: "prompt: 'Summarize invoice 9072 for the customer'
response before deploy: 'Invoice 9072 — total due $1,240. Paid on 2025-10-10.'
response after deploy: '[OLD TEMPLATE] Please check your billing portal for invoice details.'"

martin_support: They included request_ids: r_0a1b2c3d (first fail), r_0f9e8d7c (later). Ticket 7892. Customer says it started immediately after canary cut.

anya_engineer: can you paste the exact prompt + request_id + model and variant used? also which region/customer token?

martin_support: model=redwood-chat-3b, variant=quant-v2, region=us-west-2, request_id=r_0a1b2c3d. Prompt above. Token belongs to acme-corp-prod.

anya_engineer: thanks. quick guess: KV cache keying changed in the rollout (we switched serialization of the prefix key to include model_version_id instead of model_id). if prefix hashing differs across instances you can get cross-variant hits returning stale KV cache entries. canary-bot logs? @canary-bot any cache-hit anomalies for that timeframe?

canary-bot: [deploy-notice] canary 2025-11-02T14:01UTC cut.
canary-bot: [cache-stats] us-west-2 quant-v2: spike in kv_hit_rate for prefix="" at 14:02:14 UTC; observed mismatched model_version tags on 0.8% of hits.

sre_tom: that matches. i've seen alerts about unexpected key collisions from the new serializer. we also changed TTL behavior (shorter active ttl, longer background ttl) — could let older entries be returned during fallback.

runtime_jen: repro checklist: 1) use same prompt, 2) ensure warm KV cache on node A (pre-rollout state), 3) route request to node B (post-rollout keying) and observe returned cached output. i can try to reproduce locally if someone gives me the exact env and commit hash of the deploy.

martin_support: commit is a7c9f2b. i'm going to ask the customer for a repro with a single request that hits a specific request_id — they already sent r_0a1b2c3d and logs.

anya_engineer: meanwhile can we evict ACME's prefix entries from the global cache as a short mitigation? we have admin endpoint: POST /admin/cache/evict {"owner":"acme-corp-prod","prefix":""} — martin, want me to run that?

martin_support: please run it, thanks. also asked customer to test right after eviction.

anya_engineer: ran eviction at 14:04:30 UTC — response 204. noted which nodes got the invalidation.

canary-bot: [action] evict applied to nodes: node-12, node-14, node-17.

martin_support: customer confirmed at 14:06 that responses look normal again. they said: "looks fixed, thanks" :relieved:. attaching their confirmation to the ticket.

sre_tom: good. root cause likely the serialization change that altered the key namespace combined with staged TTL semantics. we need a hotfix to ensure new serializer preserves stable keying (hash prefix must be stable across canary/primary) or add migration that invalidates keys on deploy.

anya_engineer: agreed. proposed plan: 1) revert serialization change in the next patch (quick rollback) or 2) implement canonicalizer that normalizes prefix -> sha256(prefix || canonical_model_identifier) and keep it backwards compatible. also add an automatic invalidation hook during rollout so old cached entries don't survive.

runtime_jen: i'll file a PR for the canonicalizer and a migration script to backfill keys for the last 48h. canary tests will include a cross-node hit test.

martin_support: message to customer: we flushed your cache and opened a fix. they asked whether any data was lost — i told them no data loss, just stale outputs.

sre_tom: create an incident postmortem entry and tag it with customer impact + rollout config. also add a monitoring rule for mismatched model_version tags on cache hits.

anya_engineer: noted. i'll add the monitoring rule and create a canary test for key consistency.

martin_support: closing loop with customer now. thanks all :team-heart:

runtime_jen: follow-up todo: add unit test for empty-prefix edge-case and ensure serialization format is deterministic across golang/python runtimes.

anya_engineer: also add a migration endpoint to evict by owner for quick mitigations in future incidents.

martin_support: tagging ticket as resolved for now; will reopen if ACME reports recurrence.
